title: Atlas database user password in a request field
summary: A synthetic user-chosen password in the password property of a database user create request, in a raw HTTP JSON body, a single-quoted curl data argument and a JSON file. The values contain only letters and digits.
rationale: Atlas documents password as a write-only request property chosen by the caller, at least 8 characters, described as an alphanumeric string, and absent from responses. The text is user chosen and has no format, so the field name is the only identifying context and no value shape is implied. How such a password is percent-encoded when it is later placed in a connection string is not established by the cited pages and is left unresolved: no fixture contains a percent-encoded or connection-string form. The extent is the string value of the property and excludes the quotes.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#235). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Flagged under project policy: the string value of the password property of a database user request is treated as a credential. Atlas documents the write-only, caller-chosen property (carrier existence only); the value admission and extent are the project's decisions, and the percent-encoded connection-string form is left unresolved.

sources.supports: CloudDatabaseUser.password: 'Alphanumeric string that authenticates this database user against the database specified in databaseName ... This parameter doesn't appear in this response.' minLength 8, writeOnly
CloudDatabaseUser.password is a writeOnly request property: 'To authenticate with SCRAM-SHA, you must specify this parameter.'

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
